questions.q: How will David give thanks to Yahweh and of what will he tell?
questions.a: He will give thanks to Yahweh with his whole heart and tell about all his marvelous deeds.

questions.q: When David’s enemies turn back, what happens to them?
questions.a: The enemies stumble and perish before Yahweh.

questions.q: What has the righteous judge done for David?
questions.a: The righteous judge sits on his throne and has defended David’s just cause.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do to the nations and the wicked?
questions.a: He rebukes the nations, destroys the wicked, and blots out their name forever and ever.

questions.q: What happens to the enemy?
questions.a: The enemy are finished in desolation forever, and all remembrance of them perishes.

questions.q: Who sits forever and has established his throne for justice?
questions.a: Yahweh sits forever and has established his throne for justice.

questions.q: How does Yahweh judge the world and what does he do for the nations?
questions.a: Yahweh judges the world fairly and makes just decisions for the nations.

questions.q: What will Yahweh be for the oppressed?
questions.a: Yahweh will be a stronghold for the oppressed in times of trouble.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about those who know Yahweh’s name?
questions.a: Those who know Yahweh’s name trust in him, because Yahweh has not abandoned those who seek him.

questions.q: What does David say the people are to do for Yahweh, who sits in Zion?
questions.a: They are to sing praises to Yahweh and tell the nations what Yahweh has done.

questions.q: What does Yahweh not forget?
questions.a: He does not forget the cry of the poor.

questions.q: What is David asking Yahweh to do for him?
questions.a: He is asking Yahweh to have mercy on him.

questions.q: By whom is David oppressed?
questions.a: David is oppressed by those who hate him.

questions.q: Where will David rejoice in salvation?
questions.a: David will rejoice in salvation in the gates of the daughter of Zion.

questions.q: What has happened to the nations?
questions.a: The nations have sunk down into the pit that they made and their feet are caught in the net that they hid.

questions.q: Who has revealed himself and done justice?
questions.a: Yahweh has revealed himself and done justice.

questions.q: Where are the wicked sent?
questions.a: They are sent to Sheol, along with all the nations that forget God.

questions.q: What will not happen to the needy and the afflicted?
questions.a: The needy will not be forgotten forever, nor will the hope of the afflicted perish forever.

questions.q: What does David want Yahweh to prevent humanity from doing?
questions.a: David wants Yahweh to arise and not let humanity prevail.

questions.q: What is David asking Yahweh to do to the nations?
questions.a: He is asking Yahweh to terrify them and make them know that they are mere men.

commentary.text: David praises God for protecting his people.
And for cause to praise him.

Verses 1–10 If we would praise God acceptably, we must praise him in sincerity, with our whole heart. When we give thanks for some one particular mercy, we should remember former mercies. Our joy must not be in the gift, so much as in the Giver. The triumphs of the Redeemer ought to be the triumphs of the redeemed. The almighty power of God is that which the strongest and stoutest of his enemies are no way able to stand before. We are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth, and that with him there is no unrighteousness. His people may, by faith, flee to him as their Refuge, and may depend on his power and promise for their safety, so that no real hurt shall be done to them. Those who know him to be a God of truth and faithfulness, will rejoice in his word of promise, and rest upon that. Those who know him to be an everlasting Father, will trust him with their souls as their main care, and trust in him at all times, even to the end; and by constant care seek to approve themselves to him in the whole course of their lives. Who is there that would not seek him, who never hath forsaken those that seek Him?

Those who believe that God is greatly to be praised, not only desire to praise him better themselves, but desire that others may join with them. There is a day coming, when it will appear that he has not forgotten the cry of the humble; neither the cry of their blood, or the cry of their prayers. We are never brought so low, so near to death, but God can raise us up. If he has saved us from spiritual and eternal death, we may thence hope, that in all our distresses he will be a very present help to us. The overruling providence of God frequently so orders it, that persecutors and oppressors are brought to ruin by the projects they formed to destroy the people of God. Drunkards kill themselves; prodigals beggar themselves; the contentious bring mischief upon themselves: thus men's sins may be read in their punishment, and it becomes plain to all, that the destruction of sinners is of themselves. All wickedness came originally with the wicked one from hell; and those who continue in sin, must go to that place of torment. The true state, both of nations and of individuals, may be correctly estimated by this one rule, whether in their doings they remember or forget God. David encourages the people of God to wait for his salvation, though it should be long deferred. God will make it appear that he never did forget them: it is not possible he should. Strange that man, dust in his and about him, should yet need some sharp affliction, some severe visitation from God, to bring him to the knowledge of himself, and make him feel who and what he is.
